issues.title: `async` function with no `await` in its body

evidence.snippet: async function runBanditJson(root: string, timeoutMs: number, diagnostics: ExternalToolDiagnostic[]):

issues.whyItMatters: An `async` function whose body never uses `await` returns a Promise wrapping a synchronous value, forcing every caller to `await` (or `.then`) for no actual asynchrony. The signature lies about whether I/O happens, and any caller that forgets the `await` silently gets a Promise object instead of the value. AI-generated code marks helpers async "to be safe" when it has no idea whether the helper does I/O — this rule surfaces those.

suggestedFix.instructions: Either drop the `async` keyword (the function is synchronous), or add the missing `await`. If the function MUST stay async for an interface contract (e.g. it implements a method that other implementations DO await), suppress with a comment that names the interface and explains why.
verificationCriteria: The function either uses `await` in its body OR is no longer marked async
All callers continue to work (either they already awaited, or no longer need to)
Re-scan reports core-quality-async-without-await resolved for this function

issues.title: Hardcoded provider secret in source
issues.whyItMatters: Stripe live secret key detected at web/src/components/landing/InteractiveDiff.tsx:82. Treat the original token as compromised — git history preserves it even after a deletion commit.

suggestedFix.instructions:
Remove the literal token and read it from an environment variable:

  const token = process.env.STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY;
  if (!token) throw new Error('Stripe live secret key is required');

Then:
  1. Rotate the leaked token in the Stripe dashboard.
  2. Replace it everywhere with the env-var reference.
  3. Add the env-var name to .env.example without a value.
  4. Audit access logs for the period between commit and rotation.

issues.title: Empty catch block silently swallows errors
issues.whyItMatters: An empty catch turns every failure inside the try into a silent no-op. The next time the inner code throws — a network failure, an unexpected null, a write that returned EACCES — execution continues as if everything succeeded. The exact bug class that produces silent data loss in production. AI tools insert empty catches to satisfy lints or types without thinking about the actual failure mode.

verificationCriteria: The catch block now logs the error, rethrows, or returns a deliberate fallback with a comment

issues.title: Imports a package not declared in package.json (slopsquatting risk)
issues.whyItMatters: `@sentry/nextjs` is imported here but the package root `@sentry/nextjs` is not declared in the project's package.json (dependencies / devDependencies / peer / optional). One of: (a) the AI hallucinated the name and an attacker may register it on npm → slopsquatting; (b) a real package needs to be added to dependencies; (c) the name was renamed but the import wasn't updated.

suggestedFix.instructions:
Decide which case applies BEFORE running `npm install`:

  (a) HALLUCINATION — delete the import. Replace the usage with the standard library or a package that actually exists. Do NOT `npm install @sentry/nextjs` to "make the error go away" — that's exactly the slopsquatting trap.

  (b) FORGOTTEN INSTALL — add `@sentry/nextjs` to dependencies, install, and verify the npm metadata: publisher matches a known maintainer, weekly downloads > 1k, the repo URL resolves to an active project.

  (c) RENAME — update the import to the correct package name.

If your project uses path aliases (tsconfig `paths`, vite `resolve.alias`) and `@sentry/nextjs` is one of them, suppress with a Reason comment — v1 doesn't read path-alias config.
verificationCriteria: `@sentry/nextjs` is either removed from the import OR added to package.json (with verified npm metadata)
Re-scan reports vibe-supply-chain-hallucinated-import resolved for this line

Add the missing flags to the cookie options object:

  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  sameSite: 'lax',

For "secure": in development, condition on NODE_ENV so localhost still works:
  secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'
